thread:
Eva H.: quick q — attaching the latest form mock for user settings. thinking about required markers and delete confirmation for the linked apps list. sketches: asterisk + subtle 'required' label vs inline 'Required' text. also debating inline errors (per-field) vs top summary on submit. thoughts?
Mike R.: i lean inline for immediate correction, summary only when there are many errors at once. avoids scrolling back.
Chitra: agree on inline, but we need an accessible announcement (role="alert") when error appears. screen reader users miss visual-only cues.
Sam: is asterisk alone enough? a11y folks usually prefer explicit text like "(required)" so it's clear when read out.
Liz: +1 explicit text. asterisk is ambiguous across cultures. can we show asterisk visually and expose "required" to SR via aria-label?
Eva H.: good call. i prefer visual asterisk for density, and SR-only "required" copy. keeps UI compact.
Mike R.: for destructive actions (delete linked app) i mocked two options: 1) simple modal with checkbox "also delete data" + primary "Delete" 2) typed-confirmation typing the app name before button enables.
Chitra: typed-confirmation is best for high-impact deletes, but it's heavy for quick clears. maybe tier: typed for org-level delete, modal+checkbox for per-item.
Sam: performance + friction considerations. typed-confirmation increases support tickets if copy is confusing. need clear microcopy.
Liz: microcopy suggestion: `Type the app name to confirm deletion: "Redwood Sync"` and show remaining char count. keep it explicit.
Eva H.: on inline errors — propose using short verb-first messages: "Enter a valid email" vs "Email is invalid". actionable tone works better.
Mike R.: yes + include example when helpful: "Enter a valid email (e.g., name@company.com)"
Chitra: visual contrast: error text must meet AA for 14px. also icons alone aren't enough, add text and aria-describedby linking input to message.
Sam: mobile: summaries are helpful because users often submit from a scrolled position. maybe show an in-view banner with count that anchors to first error.
Liz: what about required field density? for large forms can we only mark optional fields instead to reduce clutter?
Eva H.: interesting — inverted pattern. prefer marking optional instead of required when most are required. but can be surprising. maybe only when >80% required.
aria-bot: accessibility checklist reminder: ensure focus moves to first error, errors announced, color not sole indicator, labels associated, typing confirmations accessible, and keyboard operable modals.
Mike R.: next steps: i'll update the mock with SR-only required copy, role=alert on errors, and a typed-confirm tiering doc. share back for quick review. :thumbsup:
Eva H.: thanks — aim to finalize before Friday design sync. :sparkles:
